Claim:
The Trump administration resulted in a trade deficit that was 'one of the highest we've ever seen in the history of America.'
Began: Sept 10, 2024 (ABC presidential debate) | Ended: Sept 11, 2024 (FactCheck.org: Biden-era annual deficits exceeded Trump's peak)
Notes:
BEA: 2020 Trump peak ~$654B; later Biden 12-month figures higher.
Primary record: BEA international trade data is the official series for U.S. goods-and-services deficits, against which claims that Trump left 'one of the highest' deficits in history can be checked against later larger totals.
Verification_Note: Census/BEA BOP series: 2020 goods deficit -$912.9B was the largest on record at the time (prior high 2006, -$837.3B); goods and services -$646.0B was the 5th-largest through 2020 (behind 2005-2008). "One of the highest we've ever seen" is supported by the primary record; later Biden-era deficits being higher does not make it false.
Flag: Evidence contradicts the case: the claim is substantially accurate.
